The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

Recent findings suggest that for those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

It has been revealed that leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

Sources indicate that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Industry observers note that ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not at the moment have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

It has been revealed that newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

It has been revealed that from the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Industry observers note that leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Sources indicate that newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Industry observers note that leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

It has been revealed that newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Sources indicate that two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

In a recent development, stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the fresh striker.

Industry observers note that it’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

According to recent reports, lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

It has been revealed that the start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

According to recent reports, but Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

Sources indicate that there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Recent findings suggest that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

It has been revealed that mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

It has been revealed that newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always crucial to ride the momentum as long as possible.

According to recent reports, eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Industry observers note that good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

According to recent reports, the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

In a recent development, newcastle’s sound form with their fresh model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

According to recent reports, it is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Sources indicate that joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who states that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the Newly introduced Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.
  • Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly declared his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly declared his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku declared his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

Former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan mentioned.

According to recent reports, 'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his plans, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

'16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

Industry observers note that 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

Sources indicate that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

It has been revealed that 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he remarked.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

Sources indicate that 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

  • It has been revealed that speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. The Breisgauer secured their sixth consecutive competitive victory thanks to a stoppage-time winner from Niklas Beste, with Schuster emphasizing the importance of a united dressing room in navigating a demanding schedule.

Sources indicate that the Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend.Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd. Freiburg nevertheless found another way to win. Substitute Derry Scherhant earned a penalty in the 89th minute, and fellow replacement Beste eventually converted the loose ball after Matthias Ginter’s spot kick struck the post.

It has been revealed that speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner. The 41-year-old suggested that the team’s togetherness gives him the confidence to rotate extensively without compromising Freiburg’s competitiveness.

“That scene in which the team celebrated together is emblematic of this group,” Schuster told the journalists. “That lends us the strength to rotate the squad with full confidence. One sees this with various clubs that have to deal with extreme pressure during this phase [of the season]. There’s also players who have international obligations. The pressure is extreme.

According to recent reports, “One really can’t leave anyone out,” Schuster continued. “We have this depth and there’s always little things that leave one needing to switch it up. Then it’s nice when players are ready to serve on a regular basis and not to get caught up in the competition of who makes the team sheet. That’s extremely vital and I’m very pleased with the lads who started today and were able to make a contribution to the win.”.

Schuster’s observations build on his earlier comments concerning Freiburg’s exceptional dressing-room culture. In October, the SC trainer emphasized the importance of protecting the club’s special atmosphere and ensuring that difficult personnel decisions do not undermine the collective.

In a recent development, the same philosophy has also been emphasized by Freiburg’s players. Veteran midfielder Maximilian Eggestein recently discussed the importance of sacrificing individual ambitions for the team, while Germany internationals Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant credited Freiburg’s supportive club culture when reflecting on their own development.

Goalkeeper Mio Backhaus offered a vivid account of the hectic closing stages, during which Ginter’s missed penalty eventually led to Beste’s winning goal.

It has been revealed that “Plenty of chaos,” Backhaus responded when asked about the penalty scene by Baden FM in the mixed zone afterwards. “For [Matthias] Ginter it was also a difficult situation to [take a penalty] four minutes into injury time. And then there was all this turmoil. It was pure ecstasy that Nikki [Beste] pulled that off after all the commotion.”.

According to recent reports, “The fact that there were so many of us involved, so many boots on the ground, that helped us re-orient ourselves as a cohesive unit,” Backhaus continued. “The fact that Derry [Scherhant] came on to draw the penalty and Nikki converted [both of them off the bench] also wasn’t a coincidence.”.

Beste had already made an notable contribution to Freiburg’s previous victory, setting up Igor Matanovic’s winner against Elversberg. The Croatian striker emphasized his instinctive understanding with his teammate after that match, highlighting the familiarity that has developed between Freiburg’s attacking players and the special chemistry emerging within Schuster’s squad.

Club captain Christian Günter similarly regarded the celebrations after Beste’s winning goal as a reflection of the team’s identity.

“This scene describes our season up to this point effectively,” Günter answered when asked about the celebratory scenes by Kicker’s Carsten Schröter-Lorenz in the mixed zone afterwards. “From solidarity to the fact that everyone wishes everyone else all the best. That the team stands above everything else and that we never give up. And that’s something we’ll have to embody until the very last minute of the very last matchday.”.

“Irrespective of what the situation is, we must remain positive, supportive of each other and stick together,” Günter continued. “One can see that we have the quality and have proven that we can get through games that aren’t exactly pretty and require a lot of fight. We’ve got to preserve that and then we’ll get good things and a good season.”.

Günter’s assessment closely resembles Matanovic’s recent observations about Freiburg’s growing ability to grind out difficult victories. Speaking after the narrow triumph over Elversberg, the striker explained how Freiburg have developed the resilience necessary to prevail in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Thursday’s encounter with Twente offered another example. Much like the Elversberg fixture, Freiburg struggled against an opponent that enjoyed lengthy spells of superiority but nevertheless managed to claim all three points.

It has been revealed that the victory extended Freiburg’s winning streak to six competitive matches and marked their 14th consecutive European home victory. The latter run began under former trainer Christian Streich in November 2023 and has continued under Schuster.

With Schuster able to trust both his starters and substitutes, Freiburg’s collective mentality continues to provide a foundation for their success across three competitions.

Despite watching his side concede a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 2-1 defeat, Weghorst was full of praise for the Bundesliga club’s progress.

The Schwarzwaldverein were already establishing themselves as regular contenders for European qualification during that period, but their continued progress has since carried them to even greater heights.

Sources indicate that freiburg reached their first European final last season, eventually losing to Aston Villa in the Europa League showpiece in Istanbul. The club nevertheless secured another season of European football and entered the current campaign with a revamped squad.

As Get German Football News examined extensively in our 2026/27 Freiburg tactical preview, the club’s ability to navigate significant departures, reinvest intelligently, and maintain tactical continuity has remained central to its success.

Industry observers note that freiburg’s current European campaign has offered further evidence of that progress. Following November’s hard-fought Conference League victory over Trabzonspor, Schuster’s men have now extended their remarkable home-winning streak in European competition to 14 matches.

According to recent reports, thursday’s contest against Twente was hardly straightforward. The Dutch visitors enjoyed the better of the opening half despite conceding an early goal to Cyriaque Irié. Younes Taha’s superb second-half free kick eventually brought Twente level before substitute Niklas Beste struck in stoppage time to secure Freiburg’s sixth consecutive competitive victory.

The result also kept alive the European ambitions that Schuster and Vincenzo Grifo discussed following the club’s Conference League opener against FK Jablonec. Freiburg’s supporters have made no secret of their hopes for another deep continental run after last season’s historic adventure.

For Weghorst, the progress is unmistakable. The former Bundesliga striker may have departed Freiburg empty-handed on Thursday evening, but his assessment of the club’s remarkable transformation was unequivocally positive.

Germany international Stated El Mala believes his developing partnership with Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore still has considerable room for improvement. The 20-year-old Cologne attacker has spoken enthusiastically about his understanding with the English youngster following their successful attacking combination in last weekend’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Bayern Munich.

Recent findings suggest that moore, 19, scored his first Bundesliga goal in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena, rounding Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after receiving a return pass from El Mala. The well-worked goal provided a welcome breakthrough for the Englishman following a difficult start to his loan spell in Germany.

As Get German Football News reported following the Bayern encounter, Moore expressed relief at finally opening his Bundesliga account and discussed the growing understanding between himself and El Mala.

The partnership has been a topic of considerable interest ever since Moore arrived from Tottenham in August. Cologne head coach René Wagner spoke of his enthusiasm for the attacking combination back in September, emphasizing that the two youngsters were not competing for one exclusive place in the team. Moore himself subsequently expressed his desire to develop a stronger understanding with El Mala ahead of October’s Rhein derby against Borussia Mönchengladbach.

In a recent development, the friendship also extends beyond the training ground, with El Mala revealing that his older brother Malek has spent time with Moore as well. Speaking in an extensive interview with Kicker, the 20-year-old described their growing bond.

It has been revealed that “Malek and I get on really well with Mikey,” El Mala told Kicker. “The three of us recently went out for a meal together. We get along very well. Now he’s scored his first goal after a great attacking move, which gives us confidence for the coming matches that we can play together like that. I also have a very good relationship with Linton Maina, for example, and you can see that on the pitch.”.

Cologne have struggled to translate promising performances into victories this season, but the development of their young attacking players offers encouragement. With Moore finally opening his Bundesliga account and El Mala increasingly comfortable operating in central attacking positions, Wagner will hope their growing understanding produces further rewards.

Sources indicate that there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

In a recent development, "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

In a recent development, dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second highlighted his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

In a recent development, max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a newly introduced contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” remarked Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Sources indicate that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Industry observers note that dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” mentioned Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

In a recent development, dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

In a recent development, it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

In a recent development, arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Recent findings suggest that given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

It has been revealed that the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

It has been revealed that on managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta remarked: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta stated: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. “Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

Recent findings suggest that it has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he remarked. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little problems that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:.

In a recent development, “Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”.

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:.

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies noted Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

Recent findings suggest that the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

Industry observers note that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

Recent findings suggest that and while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta stated: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

Industry observers note that when asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil stated: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

Industry observers note that good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager noted: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

Ufficiale, Captain America Pulisic è tornato. Con lui il campo il Milan va al doppio

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sarà che è girato tutto storto al Milan da febbraio in avanti l'anno scorso, sarà che il Mondiale era un peso forse troppo elevato, sarà che fisicamente non è stato sempre al top.
  • Ci ricordiamo tutti come è andata la stagione di Captain America Christian Pulisic l'anno scorso.
  • Recent findings suggest that decisiva è stata la prima sosta della stagione, in cui Pulisic è rimasto a Milanello per ritrovare la forma ideale.

Sarà che è girato tutto storto al Milan da febbraio in avanti l'anno scorso, sarà che il Mondiale era un peso forse troppo elevato, sarà che fisicamente non è stato sempre al top. Può essere tutto, ma era impossibile che Christian Pulisic avesse smesso improvvisamente di essere Captain America. Arrivati ormai agli sgoccioli del mese di novembre, ora va detto: è ufficiale Captain America Pulisic è ufficialmente tornato. E per il Milan è cruciale, perchè con l'americano in campo i rossoneri vanno al doppio.

Ci ricordiamo tutti come è andata la stagione di Captain America Christian Pulisic l'anno scorso. Nella prima metà, praticamente fino all'ultima gara di dicembre, era stato a mani basse il miglior calciatore del campionato con 10 gol stagionali (e non solo) tra campionato e Coppa Italia. Scavallato il Capodanno, l'americano si è totalmente perso. Alla lunga, il peso di non riuscire più a segnare e il rendimento oggettivamente desolante della squadra di Allegri hanno fatto il resto. Il Milan ha chiuso la stagione con l'enigma Pulisic, uno che prima era una certezza. Al Mondiale la sfortuna ha perseguitato ancora l'americano che di fatto si è infortunato due volte: nella prima partita e nell'ultima, l'ottavo di finale che ha sancito l'eliminazione degli Stati Uniti. Ed è stato proprio questo infortunio che ne ha ritardato il rientro in gruppo a Milanello per la nuova stagione. Facile ricordare come nelle prime gare della stagione Pulisic partisse sempre dalla panchina, perché Amorim non lo riteneva ancora nella condizione ideale. Poi è cambiato tutto e Pulisic è ufficialmente tornato.

Recent findings suggest that decisiva è stata la prima sosta della stagione, in cui Pulisic è rimasto a Milanello per ritrovare la forma ideale. E lo ha fatto. Già nelle ultime uscite prima della pausa aveva ritrovato il gol a San Siro contro il Lecce, il primo con il Milan nel 2026. Poi al rientro dalle Nazionali dei compagni è tornato a fare quello che sa fare meglio: essere determinante. Nello spezzone di ottobre di campionato 3 gol contro Udinese, Inter e Genoa. Al ritorno dalla seconda sosta ha aggiunto altre due reti contro Frosinone e Olympiacos. Ieri nello specifico il suo ingresso ha contribuito a risvegliare il Milan: ha offerto soluzioni diverse tra le linee e la possibilità di avere qualità nello stretto in verticale, elementi che era mancati nel primo tempo. Con il Milan ha segnato 4 gol nelle ultime 5 partite. In totale in questa stagione rossonera è già a quota 6 gol e 2 assist, a cui si aggiungono le 3 reti marcate in Nazionale. Quindi sì, è ufficiale Captain America Pulisic è tornato.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prima compagni e poi allenatore e giocatore, ora Gattuso e Abate si sfidano nelle rispettive aree tecniche.

According to recent reports, sabato pomeriggio Torino-Lazio vedrà Gennaro Gattuso e Ignazio Abate uno contro l’altro uno contro l'altro da allenatori, con i biancocelesti concentrata sul proprio percorso e i granata la cui ultima vittoria in campionato risale ormai a un mese fa. Un incrocio che riporta indietro nel tempo, al loro lungo passato condiviso al Milan prima sul campo e poi in panchina.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il loro primo incontro risale all’estate del 2009, quando Abate tornò al Milan ritrovando Gattuso già senatore del gruppo. Fino al 2012 hanno condiviso spogliatoio e campo, vincendo insieme lo Scudetto 2010-2011 e la Supercoppa Italiana, con Gattuso punto di riferimento per la crescita del compagno.

Nel novembre 2017 si sono ritrovati con Gattuso passato sulla panchina del Milan, dove si è ritrovato ad allenare un Abate ancora in campo e ormai veterano. Il rapporto è rimasto schietto e diretto, con Gattuso che ha chiesto sempre il massimo fino a schierarlo anche da difensore centrale in emergenza, prima del comune addio al club nel maggio 2019.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football.
  • Musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September.
  • Kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football. According to Kicker, the 23-year-old appears to have aggravated the muscle injury that previously sidelined him for nearly two months. The German international will consequently miss Saturday’s Bundesliga away fixture against Hamburger SV.

Musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September. After gradually working his way back to fitness, the Bayern star finally returned to competitive action in last Friday’s 1-1 draw against Köln. He also made a brief appearance in Wednesday’s 2-1 Champions League defeat against Lille.

Kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear. Fußballtransfers claims Musiala’s absence will stretch out for several more weeks. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg is reporting that Musiala will miss 4-6 weeks.

The latest development comes during an exceptionally difficult period for Musiala, who has also been dealing with a neurological condition. Kicker and Sport Bild both report that the 23-year-old experienced another absence episode on Monday, November 23, his second reported recurrence since collapsing during August’s preparation campaign. Musiala has consequently made just six competitive appearances this season, completing the full 90 minutes on only one occasion.

His ongoing health difficulties have also prompted considerable discussion surrounding his future at Bayern. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge recently expressed concerns about the midfielder’s ability to regain his previous performance levels. Earlier this week, Bayern also confirmed that constructive discussions had taken place with Musiala’s representatives. The club emphasized that the player’s health remained the priority and that both parties intended to continue their dialogue confidentially.

Industry observers note that for Kompany, Musiala’s latest absence also creates another selection headache amid a mounting injury crisis in Bayern’s attacking department. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of Saturday’s encounter with Hamburg. The French international continues to recover from bruising to his left foot sustained against Köln. Harry Kane, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari remain sidelined as well, leaving Bayern seriously depleted in attack. Luis Díaz at least returned to action against Lille following his own injury layoff.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.
  • Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are at the moment only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are at the moment only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the new rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

In a recent development, would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football demonstrates no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

ANALYSIS | Eric Smith: Meet of the 2. Bundesliga’s smartest players, and why St. Pauli need him

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ever since becoming an vital player for St.
  • Under Fabian Hürzeler, he played a hybrid role, combining the positions of centre back and holding midfielder.
  • He received a lot of praise for mastering this role, which was linked to a transfer to a bigger club, such as VfB Stuttgart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since becoming an vital player for St. Pauli, Eric Smith has enjoyed successful seasons.

Under Fabian Hürzeler, he played a hybrid role, combining the positions of centre back and holding midfielder. During those successful periods, he controlled and directed St. Pauli’s attack. His movement destroyed the opponent’s initial press and his passing cracked defensive structures, starting his team’s attack.

He received a lot of praise for mastering this role, which was linked to a transfer to a bigger club, such as VfB Stuttgart. However, he decided to stay.

According to recent reports, under Alexander Blessin, he sometimes played as a number six and more frequently as a central centre-back. Although he didn’t have the freedom to move around as much as before, he was still dictating the tempo, and his long balls played a more integral part in St. Pauli’s direct attack. However, during Blessin’s time at the club, the Kiezkicker were more passive offensively, so Smith’s role was more highlighting the defensive part.

It has been revealed that in that role, though, he delivered some good performances, especially in their first Bundesliga season, and was consistently solid defensively. Once again, he was linked with a transfer, this time to Leicester City in England. And once again, Eric Smith decided to stay.

Industry observers note that the following season, after St. Pauli were relegated to the 2. Bundesliga, there were rumours that Smith was about to leave. He was linked with Belgian giants Anderlecht, but the move never materialised.

Nevertheless, he has continued to perform well, even though his team has not been as consistent. In the summer, Graham Potter selected him for the Sweden national team at the World Cup. Even though he has shown some flaws, particularly in duels, his performances suggest that he might be too good for the 2. Bundesliga. He might be a better fit for a higher league.

And so far this season, this has been proven true. Even though St. Pauli haven’t really been consistent, Smith has been performing well from matchday to matchday.

The data also indicates this. According to Ben Griffis’s measurements, Smith is currently in the top five of the 2. Bundesliga for three different midfield roles (number six, defensive midfielder and advanced playmaker). No other midfielder can be in the top five in all of these categories.

In terms of passing and chance creation via passes in the 2. Bundesliga, he is also categorised as either elite (top 10%) or above average.

Not only that. Among 2. midfielders in the Bundesliga who have played at least 900 minutes so far this season, none are averaging more progressive passes or passes to the final third per 90 minutes than Smith. He is arguably still the best build-up player and progressor in the league. This is precisely why St. Pauli need him.

In a recent development, with all these numbers, it no longer makes sense to play Smith in the centre-back position. He is very familiar with this position, though, and Tim Eckhardt from Millernton also explained to me that one reason he is still playing in this position might due to the reason that he can provide reassurance to the defensive team, particularly the other centre-backs who don’t have as much experience as him. Smith himself also admits that he doesn’t feel as comfortable playing in the final third as he does at the back. However, he is needed more as a midfielder to support the team’s attack, an area in which St. Pauli has struggled this season.

It has been revealed that the last game against Bochum proved this. Smith not only made one assist, but also created five chances in total (the most in the game). He was everywhere, ensuring that St. Pauli’s attack ran smoothly — he is the glue holding the team’s offensive play together.

Industry observers note that after the game, he stated that his movements, particularly on the right side of the final third, were intended to help St. Pauli break through Bochum’s man-to-man defence. Smith’s intelligence was evident in his ability to anticipate where to move, where to meet or reach his teammate, and where to pass the ball. This approach was successful in breaking down Bochum’s defensive structure.

According to recent reports, this kind of vision was lacking when coach Marcel Rapp decided to play Smith as a centre-back in some games this season. With St. Pauli right now sitting in the middle of the table, that shouldn’t happen again. Smith needs to be their main creative outlet at the front.

In general, Smith is also third in terms of key passes per 90 minutes for his side this season, averaging 1.5 and only behind two playmakers Conor Metcalfe and Branimir Hrgota–which have most of their minutes playing in the final third. If these three, or at least two, players on the field together at the same time for the rest of season, St. Pauli might find the cure to solve their creative flaws.

Things also work quite well because Smith has a very good understanding with his midfield partner, Joel Fujita. The Japanese player knows how to cover ground when Smith is in the final third, and also knows when to get close to the ball when Smith needs help.

Well, they both have qualities that many would argue are better than the 2. Bundesliga level. Keeping them as a double-six duet would give St. Pauli one of the best midfield partnerships in the league.

Having a great midfield partnership, especially if both players are above league average, usually helps a team achieve better results. St. Pauli can certainly hope for this. It might slightly reduce their defensive quality, but to win a game you need to score more goals than your opponents–something that St. Pauli has really lacked this season.

It has been revealed that it may also be beneficial for their captain, David Nemeth, to take on more defensive responsibilities and become a true leader in that regard. It might also help Tomoya Ando and fresh recruit Marcus Mathisen to settle in and prove that they can become top defenders in the league.

Recent findings suggest that st. Pauli are not a middle-bottom 2. Bundesliga squad; they have players capable of elevating the team. They just need to make wiser decisions, and one of them is keeping Smith closer to the final third for the rest of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that undici gol nelle prime undici partite di Serie A, come Montella e uno in più di Milito. C'è un attaccante che ti ispira più degli altri?

Recent findings suggest that "Mi piace guardare gli attaccanti di oggi, soprattutto quelli del campionato in cui gioco. Mi piacciono le punte complete, che sanno giocare per la squadra e attaccare la profondità. In Serie A ce ne sono tante, Pio Esposito per esempio, e molti altri che adesso non riesco a nominare tutti".

Qual è la prima cosa che ti ha detto Jurić?

"È stato diretto fin dal primo giorno. Mi ha spiegato quali sono le mie qualità, cosa so fare e cosa no, e su cosa devo lavorare. Da allora ci lavoro ogni giorno, e lui non è mai soddisfatto. Per me è un bene. Mi ripete sempre che posso dare il 50% in più. Ricordo un giorno in cui mi ha detto che stavo andando molto bene, ma che avevo ancora tantissimo margine. Me lo porto sempre dietro, ed è quello su cui provo a migliorare giorno dopo giorno".

E su cosa devi migliorare, secondo lui e secondo te?

According to recent reports, "Secondo lui sul gioco spalle alla porta, per proteggere meglio il pallone. E sono d'accordo. Spesso il pallone mi arriva e lo perdo, altre volte riesco a tenerlo, ma devo essere più continuo. È questo che mi chiede, e su questo ha ragione".

Merlin Polzin will be looking for some kind of response when his Hamburg side host unbeaten Bayern Munich at the Volksparkstadion on Saturday afternoon.

His side are coming into this game on the back of a 4-0 defeat against Nordderby rivals Werder Bremen last weekend, their third loss in four league games. They have, however, won their last three Bundesliga games at home: against Cologne (2-1), VfB Stuttgart (1-0) and Borussia Mönchengladbach (3-1).

According to recent reports, with Miro Muheim sidelined with a muscular injury, Nicolás Capaldo is expected to move into midfield, which could see Mario Vušković make his Bundesliga debut. The Croatian defender returned earlier in the month after serving a four-year doping suspension – his last competitive appearance for HSV came in his team’s 1-0 2. Bundesliga defeat against Greuther Fürth in November 2022.

Elsewhere, Polzin is expected to name the same team that started in the Nordderby.

Daniel Heuer Fernandes – Sebastiaan Bornauw, Mario Vušković, Warmed Omari – Zakaria El Ouahdi, Nicolás Capaldo, Martin Adeline, David Møller Wolfe – Albert Grønbæk – Patson Daka, Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit.

In a recent development, stefano Pasquino, giornalista, si è così espresso su Tuttosport commentando la vittoria del Milan per 2-4 contro l'Olympiacos: "Non poteva che essere Atene la città dell’euro-rinascimento rossonero. Là dove il Milan berlusconiano ha vinto due Champions League - nel 1994 schiantando il Barcellona (4-0) e nel 2007 battendo 2-1 il Liverpool - d’incanto si è accesa la fiamma dopo cinquanta minuti da film dell’orrore in cui l’Olympiacos aveva segnato due gol ed era stato padrone del campo. A portare il fiammifero, l’eroe che non ti aspetti: Omari Hutchinson. L’inglese prima ha dimezzato le distanze con una rete straordinaria al termine di un “one man show”, poi ha piazzato sulla testa di Cisse (alla decima rete stagionale) il pallone del pareggio, infine ha concesso il bis innescando (con un cross di destro, non il piede migliore) Pulisic che di destro al volo ha impallinato Ortega. Sul gong - dopo che Capitan America si era divorato un gol più facile da segnare che da sbagliare - è arrivato il poker di Moreira in contropiede".

Il percorso del Milan, ricorda Pasquino, è, però, appena cominciato: "Bene, bravi ma servirà il bis tra due settimane a San Siro contro il Sunderland per mantenere vive le (comunque risicate) speranze di acciuffare la qualificazione diretta agli ottavi. Certo è che la vittoria sull’Olympiacos (che, prima di ieri, aveva perso soltanto una gara - la prima giocata in stagione - e arrivava da 12 risultati utili consecutivi) ha quanto meno rimesso le cose a posto in ottica qualificazione quanto meno ai playoff, dato che a gennaio il Milan affronterà il Levski (a Sofia) e l’Ararat-Armenia al Meazza: difficile pensare che non arrivino altri sei punti. Agli atti resta però anche lo sconcertante primo tempo in cui il Milan - fatta eccezione per il salvataggio di Pirola a porta vuota sul tiro di Cisse - mai è stato pericoloso, mostrando tutti i difetti già visti in Europa".

#153199. Stated El Mala opens up on nearly quitting football and rejecting Borussia Dortmund

Stated El Mala opens up on nearly quitting football and rejecting Borussia Dortmund

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1397 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany international Said El Mala has opened up about the setbacks, family influences, and personal decisions that have shaped his remarkable rise to prominence.
  • El Mala’s development has been extraordinary.
  • Football has always played a central role in the El Mala family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany international Said El Mala has opened up about the setbacks, family influences, and personal decisions that have shaped his remarkable rise to prominence. In an extensive interview with Kicker, the 20-year-old 1. FC Köln attacker reflected on his painful departure from Borussia Mönchengladbach’s youth academy, his unwavering determination to become a professional footballer, and his decision to reject opportunities elsewhere in favour of remaining in the cathedral city.

El Mala’s development has been extraordinary. Released from Gladbach at the age of 14, the Krefeld native subsequently worked his way through TSV Meerbusch and Viktoria Köln before establishing himself as one of the Bundesliga’s most exciting young players. His performances have since earned him a place in Jürgen Klopp’s German national team. The youngster nevertheless admits that his career came perilously close to ending before it had properly begun.

Football has always played a central role in the El Mala family. Stated’s father Mohammed previously played for Linner SV, helping the amateur club climb as high as the Landesliga. Unlike his two attacking sons, Mohammed operated primarily in central defence.

“No!” El Mala laughed when asked whether he inherited his attacking talent from his father. “My father was actually a centre-back. He played a lot as a sweeper, from what he’s told me. What I always heard from his former opponents was that he was a really unpleasant player to face. Someone you didn’t want to play against because he was so tall and quick. But our dad naturally still played a part in Malek and me both becoming attacking players.”.

It has been revealed that the brothers’ own footballing journey took them from Linner SV through KFC Uerdingen to Borussia Mönchengladbach. Their development then suffered a devastating setback when Gladbach decided to release them in 2021. As Get German Football News previously documented in our feature on El Mala’s journey from Gladbach reject to Germany international, the youngster was considered too small and physically underdeveloped to establish himself at the highest level. El Mala has now provided a deeply personal account of the experience, explaining that the coronavirus pandemic, injuries, and his physical development all contributed to the difficulties he encountered.

According to recent reports, “I was 14 when I was kicked out,” El Mala told Kicker. “During the coronavirus period, there were no opportunities to show what you could do. There were also injuries. I was physically weaker and still very small. Looking back on it today, it was a very difficult time.”.

Recent findings suggest that the decision was particularly devastating because El Mala had sacrificed much of his social life to pursue his footballing ambitions. His older brother’s encouragement ultimately helped preserve a footballing career that might otherwise have ended prematurely.

“When the news came, I didn’t know how to deal with it,” he explained. “At the academy, I’d had to neglect my friends from school because I didn’t have time to meet them after lessons or go to their birthdays. It was a completely upcoming life. The new friends were the lads from the team. Then, out of nowhere, you’re simply torn away from it. There were a few tears shed. But then Malek and I decided that we did want to carry on playing, simply for fun. Though the decision came more from Malek.”.

It has been revealed that despite the uncertainty surrounding his future, El Mala remained determined to become a professional footballer. The attacker revealed that he briefly considered following a completely different career path, but never seriously entertained the prospect of abandoning his original ambitions.

“I once wanted to become a police officer,” El Mala admitted. “But that thought promptly disappeared because I only wanted to pursue Proposal A. The teachers always told me that I needed a Plan B, but I remarked no. I’ve always been stubborn, and I’ve followed my own path. At first, it was simply about seeing Plan A through.”.

That determination eventually paid off. Following a spell at Meerbusch, El Mala earned an opportunity with Viktoria Köln, where his development accelerated under youth coach Marian Wilhelm. The winger subsequently earned a move to 1. FC Cologne, making the transition to Bundesliga football alongside his older brother.

Industry observers note that the siblings’ shared journey reached another milestone earlier this month when Malek scored his first Bundesliga goal in Cologne’s 1-1 draw against Union Berlin. The 21-year-old striker converted shortly after coming off the bench, with Noted involved in creating the equalizer.

After scoring 13 Bundesliga goals and providing five assists last season, El Mala attracted considerable transfer interest during the summer. Brentford, Brighton & Hove Albion, and Borussia Dortmund were among the clubs attempting to secure his services. Dortmund’s interest became particularly serious, with Cologne reportedly rejecting multiple offers from the Bundesliga rivals.

Industry observers note that instead of leaving, El Mala signed a new contract through 2031 and inherited the prestigious No. 10 shirt previously worn by club legends Lukas Podolski, Pierre Littbarski, and Wolfgang Overath. The German international has now explained the reasoning behind his decision.

According to recent reports, “We were actually in talks with FC the whole time,” El Mala told Kicker. “It’s no secret that I received offers and listened to them. But I couldn’t really imagine myself making any of those moves. Then we sat down together, my family, the club officials, and me, and talked. They demonstrated me something that really appealed to me: the team structure, who else they wanted to bring in, and how we wanted to play under the coach. That was what ultimately convinced me. We’ve added real quality.”.

According to recent reports, the opportunity to inherit Podolski’s famous shirt number also played an key role. As GGFN reported following El Mala’s first Bundesliga home appearance in the iconic shirt, the youngster has acknowledged the considerable expectations that accompany his upcoming status in Cologne. His brother’s future also influenced his decision to remain.

Sources indicate that the attacker’s mother Sabrina, who also acts as his agent, was closely involved in the discussions. El Mala stressed that the family’s decision was ultimately based on their shared conviction that remaining in Cologne represented the best next step in his development.

Recent findings suggest that “I chose Cologne,” El Mala emphasized. “I’ve felt incredibly comfortable with the lads from the very first day. We brought in a lot of newly introduced players over the summer and lost quite a few, but we haven’t lost quality. We’ve actually gained it. My brother was also one of the reasons, because I was certain he would get his opportunity this year and that things would finally click for him. The fact that it worked out and he scored straight away in Berlin made me all the happier.”.

Recent findings suggest that el Mala’s confidence in the club’s sporting direction also extends to head coach René Wagner, whose position has come under increasing scrutiny following Köln’s difficult start to the Bundesliga campaign. With just ten points from their opening ten league matches, the Rhineland club have struggled for consistency. Wagner has faced considerable criticism from sections of the support, with thousands of fans chanting for his dismissal following the recent goalless draw against Schalke. Wagner’s position had already become a subject of debate earlier in the season.

El Mala nevertheless remains firmly behind his trainer. The German international highlighted Wagner’s communication skills and individual attention to players, revealing that the coach regularly invites him to his office to review running statistics and video footage of his performances. The 20-year-old also cited Köln’s recent 1-1 draw away against Bayern Munich as evidence that Wagner and his coaching staff remain capable of preparing the team to compete with the Bundesliga’s strongest opponents.

“Everyone has a good relationship with him,” El Mala told Kicker. “He talks a lot with all of us, which is particularly key when you’re not playing or when you’re trying to improve. We work with video analysis very frequently. There are many things that distinguish him. We played a great game against Bayern. The entire coaching staff worked out a great match blueprint, which we implemented really well. If we function like that, all together as a team, we can compete against any other team and deliver that kind of performance in every match. I don’t presently see any reason to criticize the coach.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
