  • Jude Bellingham has more than settled into his routine in Madrid, with the England star learning Spanish, integrating into his community and spending time with his girlfriend in a mansion worth a reported £5.3million ($7m) after three seasons at Real Madrid.
  • The 23-year-old's settled life in the Spanish capital is thought to play a significant role in Bellingham's decision to sign an improved deal with the club, with Daily Mail Sport reporting on Monday that the midfielder is set to become one of Europe's highest earners.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 06:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 24 November 2026.

Jude Bellingham has more than settled into his routine in Madrid, with the England star learning Spanish, integrating into his community and spending time with his girlfriend in a mansion worth a reported £5.3million ($7m) after three seasons at Real Madrid.

The 23-year-old's settled life in the Spanish capital is thought to play a significant role in Bellingham's decision to sign an improved deal with the club, with Daily Mail Sport reporting on Monday that the midfielder is set to become one of Europe's highest earners.

Latest terms would see Bellingham raking in around £12.5million a year after tax until 2029, and will reportedly put him on par with his team-mate Vinicius Junior, whose latest deal is thought to be worth around £500,000 per week after tax.

But beyond the money, Bellingham has been flourishing turning out for the Spanish giants – both on and off the pitch.

Here, Daily Mail Sport details Bellingham's lifestyle in Spain, and the rituals that have grounded the player after his explosion into superstardom.

Jude Bellingham is inching closer to a fresh deal at Real Madrid to become one of Europe's highest earners.

But more than just enjoying his football, Bellingham has made himself at home in the city (pictured at the Grand Prix of Spain in Madrid this year).

A recurring theme when Bellingham speaks of his love of living in Madrid stems from an established daily routine.

Speaking to his club just six months after he joined Los Blancos in the summer of 2023, Bellingham had already set up habits which helped him feel at home in the new city.

It has been revealed that 'I get up early to go to training, I train and then I head home,' Bellingham remarked. 'Sometimes I'll go out for a coffee near home or head into town to grab something to eat. Then I go back home to chill out in the garden for a bit if the weather is good and the sun's out.

It has been revealed that 'If my friends are over, we'll go out for dinner and then back home. It's great. You get to know the people at the places you visit more often. They don't see you as Jude Bellingham the footballer, but as Jude the guy who comes in for a coffee and that's great. The people I meet in the city really look after me. I feel at home.'.

Industry observers note that over two years later, and the patterns are no different. The Calvin Klein ambassador told Vogue this month that his ideal downtime involves 'being in the company of my friends and family, having a coffee, going for a walk.

'You're always going to get recognised, but you're a bit safer in terms of not getting mobbed,' Bellingham noted of his favourite spots on the fringes of the city, where many of his repeat haunts are located.

In a recent development, not that Bellingham is a little averse to integrating with the community. In fact, mingling with the locals has been a positive aspect of Bellingham's life abroad, with the player admitting in the summer of 2025 that Spain was very much 'home'.

'When I go back to play with the national team, it's nice seeing people that I don't normally get to see – my family and friends – but I always feel more comfortable when I'm back in Madrid,' Bellingham said in an interview with FIFA. 'It's the weather, the people are so loving, the food.

'You mix all that together, as well as, especially, playing for Real Madrid… When you go out in public and the people see you, you see it's like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that they've had to meet you.

'They talk to you about the club and how much it means to them. A lot of the older ladies give me kisses on the cheeks and stuff like that! It's really nice.'.

Bellingham has connected with new head coach Jose Mourinho since his arrival in the summer.

Shortly after his move to Madrid Bellingham moved into a villa within the upscale complex at La Finca (flats inside the community pictured).

Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashyn Castro enjoy a life of habits when together in Madrid, involving coffee walks and going out for dinner (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

The 23-year-old lives in his mansion with his mother Denise, who often drives him to training as he is without a license.

Shortly after moving to Spain, Bellingham settled down in the exclusive La Finca neighbourhood, which plays host to a number of his team-mates including Kylian Mbappe and former club legends such as Zinedine Zidane, Cristiano Ronaldo and Iker Casillas.

The gated community is known as 'Madrid's Beverly Hills' to insiders and boasts extensive security to ensure the luxury villas inside the compound stay safe.

Bellingham is believed to have purchased his pricey six-bedroom home in 2023, moving into the complex, which boasts a home theatre, outdoor pool and gym according to Architectural Digest, with his mother Denise.

From there, his mum drives him to and from training, with the young star admitting in Vogue that despite his prodigious footballing talent, he remains borderline incapable in other aspects of life.

In a recent development, 'I can't cook, I can't drive… I'm good at what I do, but everything else?' he joked. 'Not that great.

According to recent reports, 'I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That's where I'm at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I've probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there'll be a time and a place for that, I'm sure.'.

In keeping with the idea that Bellingham has found his home in Spain, it stands to reason that the player has been working on his languages.

Bellingham revealed in Vogue that he has been learning Spanish for over two years, beginning in earnest just months after his move to the Santiago Bernabeu.

Confirming his aptitude for the language, Bellingham added: 'I think a massive part of it is being confident enough to just speak.

'You know you're going to get stuff wrong, and you're probably not going to sound exactly right, (but if) people know what you're talking about, they'll probably think: "Fair play for trying".'.

Castro and Bellingham have been dating for nearly two years since early 2025, having reportedly met on exclusive dating site Raya (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

American model Castro is a frequent fixture in the stands whether Bellingham is playing for Madrid or England.

With Bellingham settled in Madrid, his American model girlfriend Ashlyn Castro is, if not permanently based in the city, a regular visitor to both his La Finca villa and Real Madrid's home ground.

The former music video star and Bellingham have been dating since early 2025, with Castro becoming a frequent fixture at the Bernabeu alongside his mother Denise.

Castro has also been following his exploits for England too, travelling across the United States to follow the travails of Thomas Tuchel and Co as they reached the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup.

Most recently she was spotted in the stands closer to home however, with Bellingham and Castro snapped embracing after the final whistle blew on England's impressive win against Spain at Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • TSG Hoffenheim have officially appealed the four-match suspension handed to Turkish international Ozan Kabak following his dismissal against Eintracht Frankfurt.
  • Kabak received a straight red card in stoppage time after grabbing and pushing Frankfurt midfielder Oscar Højlund in retaliation for a heavy challenge.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Kraichgauer hope to have the suspension reduced to three matches, which would allow Kabak to return for their final league encounter of 2026 against Union Berlin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TSG Hoffenheim have officially appealed the four-match suspension handed to Turkish international Ozan Kabak following his dismissal against Eintracht Frankfurt. According to Kicker, the 26-year-old defender’s case will be heard by the DFB sports court on Friday, December 4.

Kabak received a straight red card in stoppage time after grabbing and pushing Frankfurt midfielder Oscar Højlund in retaliation for a heavy challenge. The subsequent four-match ban would rule the centre-back out of Hoffenheim’s remaining Bundesliga fixtures before the winter break.

Recent findings suggest that the Kraichgauer hope to have the suspension reduced to three matches, which would allow Kabak to return for their final league encounter of 2026 against Union Berlin. The DFB sports court could nevertheless also impose a harsher punishment following the hearing.

The appeal comes at a particularly difficult time for head coach Christian Ilzer, who has just one fit specialist centre-back available in Koki Machida. Dutch midfielder Wouter Burger had been considered as a potential emergency replacement, but suffered an abdominal muscle injury during Thursday’s Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz.

Ilzer has nevertheless emphasized that Kabak retains his full confidence despite the disciplinary incident.

According to recent reports, “Ozan is someone I really enjoy working with,” Ilzer remarked after the Europa League tie. “He’s extremely reliable and always gives everything he has in a match. I’ve discussed it with him at length, and there has also been a consequence. Nevertheless, Ozan won’t lose my trust. He doesn’t need to make amends. He simply needs to learn from this situation.”.

Kabak will begin serving his suspension when Hoffenheim host Augsburg on Sunday evening.

Come si legge dal comunicato della Lazio con la lettera di Lotito riportata dal Corriere dello Sport, quest'anno l'invito per i tesserati della Lazio è per sabato 19 dicembre alle 15.00 per celebrare la messa di Natale. il Natale è soprattutto un momento per stare insieme, ritrovarsi e ricordare ciò che conta davvero.

Quest’anno abbiamo pensato di scambiarci gli auguri in un modo diverso, più semplice, ma forse proprio per questo ancora più significativo.

Sabato 19 dicembre 2026, alle ore 15:00, ci ritroveremo nella parrocchia San Tommaso Moro, di Don Gabriele, nel quartiere San Lorenzo a Roma, per celebrare insieme la Santa Messa di Natale. Vorrei che fosse un momento per tutti noi, per sentirci parte di una comunità che ogni giorno condivide lavoro, impegno, responsabilità, gioie e difficoltà. Perché la Lazio, prima ancora di essere una società sportiva, è fatta di persone.

Quest’anno abbiamo anche deciso di vivere lo spirito del Natale attraverso un gesto concreto di solidarietà, destinando risorse al sostegno di alcune realtà della nostra città che ogni giorno si impegnano ad aiutare le persone e le famiglie che vivono situazioni di difficoltà.

Ci sono tante persone e tante famiglie che stanno attraversando momenti complicati. Credo che il modo migliore per vivere lo spirito del Natale sia anche quello di pensare a loro, rinunciando a qualcosa per noi per poter offrire qualcosa agli altri.

Non sarà un gesto che risolverà tutti i problemi, ma sarà il nostro modo di esserci, concretamente.

In a recent development, mi piacerebbe davvero che il 19 dicembre fossimo tutti presenti. Non per un appuntamento formale, ma per il piacere di ritrovarci, guardarci negli occhi, scambiarci gli auguri e condividere un momento che appartiene a tutti noi.

Perché essere una comunità significa anche questo: sentirsi parte di qualcosa e sapere che, insieme, possiamo fare del bene.

Vi aspetto e, fin da ora, auguro a voi e alle vostre famiglie un Natale sereno, con l’auspicio che il nuovo anno possa portare salute, pace e soddisfazioni.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

It has been revealed that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

It has been revealed that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

It has been revealed that “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

In a recent development, rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Substantial save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

Sources indicate that for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

Recent findings suggest that “I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Industry observers note that pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Sources indicate that is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he highlighted two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

Recent findings suggest that his mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

Sources indicate that his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some vital saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Sources indicate that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

Sources indicate that he was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc.

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

According to recent reports, we are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

This will be the final moment of the half.

Senesi absolutely clatters into McConnell but somehow escapes without a booking. There have been a number of soft yellows in this first yet one of the most blatant yellows is not given as a booking.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

According to recent reports, marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

It has been revealed that that is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

In a recent development, mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Sources indicate that liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

There is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

That is a massive chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

What a goal......that would of been! 🫢Kudus fires over what would of been a sensational move from Spurs#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/a1TPzKyJlP.

It has been revealed that gomez gives the ball away cheaply inside his own half before McConnell is penalised for a foul on Marmoush. Will Tottenham cross it or take the shot on from around 25 yards out? The answer is the latter and Marmoush goes for goal but misses the target.

Sources indicate that that was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a latest contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Industry observers note that koumas comes close to putting Liverpool in front with their first real chance of the game. Ngumoha slides a clinical pass into the box to pick out the run in behind of Koumas, who gets the better of Senesi. Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

Close for Lewis Koumas!The Liverpool youngster is denied by Martin Dubravka after some brilliant play by Rio Ngumoha 🪄 pic.twitter.com/YNC8QEAGGG.

Given their team has been bang average this season, the huge number of travelling Spurs fans are making a magnificent noise. They could have celebrated a long-overdue goal had it not been for a magnificent save by Giorgi Mamardashvili. The Georgian needed to make it from Lucas Bergvall, as a minute beforehand he dithered while Joe Gomez was shepherding a ball back to him and those on the Kop lost their minds. It’s tense amongst Liverpool supporters. You wonder how it changes.

That is a fantastic save from Mamardashvili. Gallagher plays the ball to Udogie on the left side of the box and the latter squares it to Bergvall in the centre of the box. Bergvall is no more than eight yards out and must think he is going to score but Mamardashvili makes a great save to deny the Swede. Should Bergvall have given Mamardashvili the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Recent findings suggest that significant save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Tottenham are dominating possession thus far, with a lot of the game being played in Liverpool’s half at the moment.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Kudus keeps it alive and sends in another cross that ends up in Mamardashvili’s arms.

We are under way at Anfield, with a place in the fourth round at stake.

A reminder, there is no extra time so it the game is all square after 90 minutes we will go straight to penalties. Also, there is no VAR tonight.

According to recent reports, both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. In Virgil van Dijk’s absence, Joe Gomez captains Liverpool tonight. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

Andrew Robertson played nearly 400 games for Liverpool and won countless trophies with the club, including two Premier League titles, two League Cups and the Champions League. Upon his return to Anfield, he starts on the bench against his former employers.

Djaksparo is a rising musician from Paris who who gained viral fame following a social media boost from Liverpool’s summer signing Bradley Barcola, who is on the bench for the hosts this evening.

“There is no joy watching Spurs at the moment. Last year was a survival job, but now you have got to flip it. [Roberto] De Zerbi’s got a lot of players at his disposal.

“He has got to fit that jigsaw puzzle together. There are still a lot of elements that are not right; they have not got a left-sided player they can trust in. Goals have been a real problem, but I do think they will come.”.

During the Spaniard’s three seasons at the helm at Bournemouth, he never made it past the fourth round in this competition. He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Industry observers note that just one player remains from Liverpool’s starting XI against Fulham on Saturday and that is Ronald Araujo. Virgil van Dijk and Florian Wirtz are given the night off for the home side.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is latest, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

In a recent development, tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi mentioned. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have significant confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I remarked we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

Unusual Mikey Moore loan clause could save Cologne €1.5m

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (375 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, FC Cologne could end up paying virtually nothing in loan fees for Tottenham Hotspur attacker Mikey Moore thanks to an unusual clause in the 19-year-old’s agreement.
  • Sources indicate that moore’s season-long loan could theoretically cost Cologne as much as €1.5 million in loan fees.
  • It has been revealed that cologne would then effectively be responsible only for the player’s wages.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, FC Cologne could end up paying virtually nothing in loan fees for Tottenham Hotspur attacker Mikey Moore thanks to an unusual clause in the 19-year-old’s agreement. According to a report appearing in the Wednesday print edition of Sport Bild, the Bundesliga club’s financial obligations decrease considerably depending on how frequently the English youngster features for René Wagner’s team.

Sources indicate that moore’s season-long loan could theoretically cost Cologne as much as €1.5 million in loan fees. The agreement nevertheless contains a provision that reduces the fee with each qualifying appearance. Should Moore make 28 competitive appearances featuring at least 45 minutes on the pitch, the payment to Tottenham would drop to its lowest possible level.

It has been revealed that cologne would then effectively be responsible only for the player’s wages. As of Wednesday, November 25, Moore had already accumulated eight appearances meeting the required playing-time threshold.

According to recent reports, the arrangement provides an obvious incentive for Cologne to continue giving Moore regular playing time, while Tottenham stand to benefit from the youngster gaining valuable Bundesliga experience. Cologne did not negotiate a purchase option as part of the agreement. Tottenham reportedly intend to incorporate the England youth international into their first-team aims for the 2027/28 campaign.

Sources indicate that the latest revelations also offer additional context to recent speculation concerning a possible premature termination of Moore’s loan. Cologne sporting director Thomas Kessler and head coach René Wagner have consistently emphasized their confidence in the youngster despite his initial difficulties adapting to German football.

According to recent reports, that patience finally began to pay dividends last Friday when Moore scored his first Bundesliga goal in Cologne’s impressive 1-1 draw against Bayern Munich. The teenager rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after combining with Said El Mala to give the visitors an early lead. Moore subsequently spoke of his relief at ending his wait for a Bundesliga goal, while El Mala expressed optimism about the pair’s developing attacking partnership.

With Moore showing signs of improvement, the financial structure of his loan offers Cologne another reason to continue investing in his development. Tottenham, meanwhile, stand to regain a more experienced player next summer without having surrendered control over his long-term future.

Giovanni Capuano, giornalista, si è così espresso su Panorama commentando le vittorie del Milan e della Juventus in Europa League: "Tre rimonte per tre vittorie, tutte importanti seppure in modo differente per Amorim, Spalletti e Sarri. Le altre del calcio italiano completano alla perfezione il lavoro cominciato dalle grandi in Champions League: 5 vittorie e 2 pareggi di peso enorme contro Psg e Manchester City compongono il bilancio di una settimana che consente alla Serie A di rialzare la testa dopo essere passata attraverso l'umiliazione del poker di sconfitte di metà ottobre.

Industry observers note that non eravamo morti allora, non siamo diventati dei fenomeni adesso. Semplicemente c'è della qualità anche dalle nostre parti e, a differenza del passato, c'è anche il rifiuto a ritenere Europa e Conference League solo come una scocciatura di metà settimana. Solo così si può spiegare la foga messa da Milan e Atalanta per ribaltare il doppio svantaggio in Grecia e Serbia mentre la Juventus si è prima complicata la vita e poi si è distesa con i ciprioti".

"Non erano - ha spiegato Giovanni Capuano - avversari di primissimo livello, erano trappole che rischiavano di scattare. Nel caso del Milan, l'Olympiacos spaventava per vecchi ricordi e perché avanti di due gol ha mostrato ai rossoneri lo spettro di una cacciata precoce dall'Europa di riserva che sarebbe stata umiliante per la storia del Diavolo. "Questa sono vittorie che svoltano la stagione" ha detto Amorim e rischia di avere ragione. Per una volta, l'uomo del match è venuto da quelle che sono considerate le seconde linee: Omari Hutchinson ha vissuto una serata di gloria allungando la sua ombra anche sulle scelte del mercato di gennaio.

According to recent reports, spalletti cercava un'affermazione con la Juventus "giusta", quella con in campo gli esterni che riempiono la sua rosa. Non tutto è filato liscio perché a tratti la manovra bianconera è stata lenta e prevedibile come troppe volte in questa stagione, poi però la scossa è arrivata dal contestato Cambiaso e da Ekhator che debuttava da centravanti. Qualità sufficiente per piegare l'Omonia Nicosia, domenica contro il Como di Fabregas servirà certamente di più".

Il paragone con Robben riguarda dunque Isaksen, mentre il giudizio positivo si estende al gioco dell’intera squadra.

In a recent development, parlando della Roma, Longhi ha definito inatteso il segnale arrivato dalla squadra. Ha richiamato City-Napoli, partita in cui a suo giudizio aveva prevalso il tatticismo, e l’ha contrapposta alla gara giocata a viso aperto sul campo del PSG, che nelle sue parole domina da due anni in Champions. La Roma, ha osservato, ha affrontato l’impegno come se avesse davanti un’altra squadra di Serie A.

Longhi ha descritto la formazione giallorossa attraverso forza, temperamento, pressing e tecnica. Di Gasperini ha detto che ha giocato sul campo del PSG scegliendo i calciatori da impiegare senza preoccupazioni: per lui è il segnale di una rosa adatta a qualsiasi tipo di impegno.

In a recent development, sull’Inter il giudizio è diverso: «Ha disputato 17 partite e non si è mai vista l'Inter come lo scorso anno o di due anni fa, per vari motivi. L'Inter rimane forte, però rimane indecifrabile.» Per questo, nel confronto di campionato, Longhi indica più la Roma dei nerazzurri.

Secondo quanto riporta il giornalista spagnolo, Alberto Pereiro, Denzel Dumfries è sempre più frustrato dai pochi minuti che José Mourinho gli ha concesso fin qui. Il nazionale olandese è arrivato dall'Inter la scorsa estate per 20 milioni di euro, ma ha visto che Federico Valverde gli viene sempre più spesso preferito come terzino destro.

According to recent reports, pereiro ha dichiarato a Onda Cero che la situazione attuale non corrisponde affatto al quadro delineato durante la trattativa. "Dumfries è un po' infastidito. Non è quello che gli era stato promesso", afferma il giornalista. Secondo Pereiro, la dirigenza sportiva del Real Madrid aveva previsto un ruolo più importante per il terzino.

Di recente, Valverde è stato preferito per la fascia destra. Mourinho sceglie costantemente di schierare il centrocampista come terzino destro, relegando di fatto Dumfries in secondo piano. Sebbene inizialmente l'olandese avesse superato Trent Alexander-Arnold nella corsa al posto da titolare, ora Valverde sembra aver superato entrambi nelle gerarchie.
